claim: @beep/mcp-kit's only Effect-MCP registration fork is sanitizedToolkit in SanitizedSpan.ts; it excludes McpServerClient from handler services and is documented as a drop-in for McpServer.toolkit.
Snapshot McpServer.toolkit/registerToolkit exclude McpRequestContext, not McpServerClient; addTool.handle R is McpRequestContext. The kit signature is no longer a type-level drop-in.
McpServer.callTool still requires McpServerClient and builds invocations via invocationFromClient, so direct callTool tests cannot type a 2026-07-28 client.

McpServerClient.protocolVersion is StatefulProtocolVersion, which excludes "2026-07-28". rc.115 used ProtocolVersion (all dated revisions). Existing stubs pin "2025-06-18" and still typecheck; they cannot name the G4 protocol.

2026-07-28 tools/call uses invocationFromRequestContext, which does not set serverClient; provideInvocationContext therefore does not provide McpServerClient. Kit Effect.serviceOption(McpServerClient) is always None on that path, so CurrentMcpCaller is never minted.

mcp-session-id is minted only on the stateful HTTP initialize path. v2026_07_28 is StatelessRuntimeDescriptor with no initialize handler; a 2026-07-28-only runtime never issues the header. Kit sessionId reads that header and documents it as the only stable per-session key.

A v2026_07_28-only HTTP runtime requires MCP-Protocol-Version, request _meta protocolVersion and clientCapabilities, Mcp-Method, and for tools/call Mcp-Name; accepted stateless requests have binding undefined (no session). Session-era initialize without those headers is rejected, not negotiated.

Every in-repo McpServerClient.of / makeStubMcpClient fixture pins protocolVersion "2025-06-18" and initializePayload.protocolVersion "2025-06-18" as never, with getClient as never. Sites: mcp-kit fixture, SanitizedToolkit.test, nlp-mcp and m365-mcp SanitizedSpan tests, uspto-mcp, gov-legal-mcp, law-practice PracticeKg.projections.

Toolkit.handle still annotates {tool, parameters} onto the current span at snapshot Toolkit.ts:336-339. registerToolkit still has no dispatch-wrapping seam. sanitizedToolkit remains the only in-repo fix for that leak.

Snapshot registerToolkit sets isError from result.isFailure and drops structuredContent on failure; parameter-origin failures become InvalidParams. Kit sets isError false for ApiKeyRequiredFailure, keeps structuredContent, and maps param errors to a canned isError CallToolResult.

The api_key_required envelope's product contract is isError:false with the encoded failure in content[].text. Adopting snapshot registerToolkit without a replacement special-case would flip that to isError:true and omit structuredContent.
Snapshot registerToolkit always sets outputSchema from tool.successSchema via ToolOutputJson and applies Tool.getStrictMode decodeOptions. Kit sanitizedToolkit sets neither.

McpSchema.ToolJson still requires top-level type:"object". Snapshot inlines a top-level $ref via resolveTopLevelReference before ToolJson decode. Kit still patches $ref schemas by spreading type:"object" for object, anyOf-object, and {not:{type:"null"}} encodings. Exact empty-class JSON Schema at the snapshot is UNVERIFIED.

Server instructions, HTTP allowedOrigins Origin checks, and four tool-hint annotations are provided upstream. Kit does not implement instructions or Origin; annotateFourHints remains a convenience. OntologyMcpTransport already passes allowedOrigins.

EnabledWhen still only affects list visibility (snapshot isVisible on register). dispatchWithTierGate remains the tools/call enforcement boundary; withEnabledWhenApprovedTool still annotates McpSchema.EnabledWhen. Kit comments citing filterByClient are stale.

SourceAuth, FieldTier, ToolkitComposition, and Version have no Effect MCP imports and do not themselves break at the snapshot. ToolkitComposition tests still call McpServer.toolkit plus StubMcpClientLayer/callTool, so they inherit the client-stub break.

README pins effect@4.0.0-beta.92 and MCP 2025-06-18; live catalog pin is 4.0.0-rc.115. AGENTS.md and McpCaller JSDoc treat mcp-session-id as the only stable per-session key. SanitizedSpan/ApiKeyRequired/TierGate module docs cite stale Toolkit.ts and McpServer.ts line numbers.

JSDoc inventory lists @beep/mcp-kit as needs-remediation: 10 public modules, 64 public exports, 75 no-root-package-import example findings, 8 multiple-description-paragraphs, 4 invalid-when-to-use-prefix. A protocol rewrite retouches SanitizedSpan, McpCaller, ApiKeyRequired, and TierGate inventory rows. Named in-source vitest example is withSanitizedToolSpan "Run under sanitized span".

SanitizedToolkit tests assert mcp-session-id header plumbing, isError:true with structuredContent for typed failures, canned boundary text for invalid params, and top-level inputSchema.type object. Coverage ratchet hottest file is SanitizedSpan.ts at 86.36% lines / 9 uncovered.

omitRequestServices at the snapshot strips McpRequestContext, McpServerClient, HttpServerRequest, and CurrentLogLevel from captured handler context. Kit captures full build-time context and provideContext-merges it, reading the session header before that provide.

McpRequestContext is the protocol-neutral request service (clientId, protocolVersion as string, optional clientInfo) and explicitly does not imply an initialized session. That is the replacement identity source for a 2026-07-28-only server; field semantics belong to 11-u2.
failureMode:"return" and Tool.getJsonSchema still exist at the snapshot, so ApiKeyRequired's Tool.make shape and kit's getJsonSchema call are not compile-broken by those APIs disappearing.

Live sanitizedToolkit consumers include nlp-mcp, m365-mcp, uspto-mcp, gov-legal-mcp, law-practice/server, and OntologyMcpTransport; those hosts currently pass protocols:[McpProtocol.v2025_06_18]. Host protocol lists belong to 21-r2.
